description.value: Investigation of brain activation during audiospatial working-memory processing using an fMRI n-back task with 1-back, 2-back and 3-back memory-load levels, with a control comparison of auditory and visuospatial 2-back tasks.

spans.text: To investigate brain mechanisms of sound location memory, we studied the distribution of brain activation with functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) in subjects performing an audiospatial n-back task with three memory load levels.

description.value: Within-subject fMRI study of healthy young adults performing audiospatial n-back tasks at three memory-load levels, with a separate auditory-versus-visual 2-back control experiment.

description.value: Auditory spatial working-memory task using binaurally presented sinusoidal tones representing left, middle and right sound locations. Participants performed 1-back, 2-back and 3-back tasks and responded after each stimulus.

spans.text: The stimulus was a sinusoidal tone (2250 Hz, duration 100 ms, interstimulus interval 3000 ms) presented through plastic tubes inserted into the earcanals through hearing protector plugs (Eartips, Nicolet Biomedical Inc., Madison, WI, USA).

description.value: Audiospatial working-memory condition requiring comparison with the immediately preceding stimulus.

spans.text: In the 1-back task the subject was instructed to press the left button whenever the stimulus was in the same location (left, middle or right) as the previous one and, when in any other location, the right button.

description.value: Audiospatial working-memory condition requiring comparison with the stimulus two trials earlier.

spans.text: In the 2-back task the subject pressed the left button when the stimulus was in the same location as the one two trials back

description.value: Audiospatial working-memory condition requiring comparison with the stimulus three trials earlier.

spans.text: in the 3-back task when in the same location as the one three trials back.

instructions.value: Press the left button when the current sound location matched the location n trials previously; otherwise press the right button.

spans.text: In the 2-back task the subject pressed the left button when the stimulus was in the same location as the one two trials back, and in the 3-back task when in the same location as the one three trials back. For all other stimuli, the subject pressed the right button.

stimuli.value: 100-ms sinusoidal tones at 2250 Hz presented binaurally through plastic tubes, with interaural intensity differences representing left and right locations and equal intensity representing the middle location.

spans.text: The stimulus was a sinusoidal tone (2250 Hz, duration 100 ms, interstimulus interval 3000 ms) presented through plastic tubes inserted into the earcanals through hearing protector plugs (Eartips, Nicolet Biomedical Inc., Madison, WI, USA). Tones were presented binaurally with an interaural intensity difference of 11 dB to mimic the right and left locations and with an equal intensity to mimic the middle location.
The subjects responded after each stimulus by pressing with the right index or middle finger the left or right button, respectively, on a response pad.

The reaction times, the number of incorrect responses and the subjective evaluations of difficulty levels in the 1-, 2- and 3-back tasks were analyzed statistically using an analysis of variance for repeated measures (ANOVA)
